column2: On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) said: “Part of the excellence of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him.” A ḥasan hadith, reported by al-Tirmidhī and others in this way.
Mā lā yaʿnīhi (“what does not concern him”): with fatḥah on the yāʾ of the present tense, from ʿanāhu al-amr, when one's attention is attached to the matter and it is part of one's aim and wish.

Part of the ugliness of a person's Islam is his engaging in what does not concern him, which is meddling in all its various kinds; for occupying oneself with it wastes precious time, whose loss can never be made up, on what one was not created for.

Encouragement to busy oneself with what concerns one, which is what a person wins in his Hereafter through Islam, faith and excellence, and what relates to the necessities of his life and livelihood; for whoever is busy with this is safe from disputes and all evils.
